doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Self-taught arranging and writing in concert key
summary: He never had arranging lessons, knew instrumentation by ear, and writes scores in concert pitch.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Were you able to ask your uncles about this arranging, like gee a tenor sax sounds — where does it sound actually on the staff and the minutiae of arranging and knowing how to use instruments?

I mean it sounds awful to say, but it was just something I always knew. I mean even when I was seven years old I would hear maybe a symphony and go, “Oh, there’s a bassoon doubling the cellos but it stops after eight bars.” “Oh hello, there’s a flute and a clarinet in octave unisons.” So I never had an arranging lesson in my life and I didn’t read a book. I mean I eventually got a book just to make sure what on earth I was doing might work, and I just looked in the book, I think it’s the Walter Piston book, and I went well hang on a minute, I know that. Well I do that anyway. Well why am I reading the book?
Like the piano lesson. “You’re doing this wrong.” But did you, at that time you would have been using a pencil and a score pad.
Did you write your scores in concert key or were they transposed already?
No I wrote them in concert. I still do.
